title: MIP starts from last cycle's plan

questions.stem: This year's budgets were cut, and a planner hands last year's approved plan, unchanged, to HiGHS as a complete start. The log shows 'User-supplied values of discrete variables cannot yield feasible solution', and the solve runs on to optimality. What became of the start?

options.text: HiGHS took it as its first incumbent and then improved on it
options.says: That log line is HiGHS rejecting the start; it never became an incumbent.

options.text: HiGHS dropped it, and the search ran as if none had been given
options.says: Right: HiGHS rejected the infeasible start, and its run was the same as with no start.

options.text: HiGHS repaired it into the nearest plan and searched from that
options.says: Gurobi tries a repair ('Another try with MIP start'); HiGHS rejected this start in one line.

options.text: HiGHS added it as rows, so this year's optimum moved toward it
options.says: A start is never a row: it cannot change which plans are allowed or which is optimal.

origin.section: Each Solver Says in Its Own Words Whether It Took the Start

questions.stem: A teammate posts: 'With last cycle's plan as a start, SCIP proved this month's model in 6,100 LP iterations instead of 7,400, so starts make SCIP 18% faster.' What should you ask for before believing the 18%?

options.text: The same single run repeated, since an iteration count needs no other models
options.says: A repeat shows the count is stable, not that the effect holds on other models or seeds.

options.text: The wall-clock seconds of both runs, since iterations understate what a start saves
options.says: Seconds change on every run; the lesson measures deterministic work for that reason.

options.text: The pairs over a fixed set of models and several seeds, summarized as a ratio
options.says: Right: one run or one seed can show a speed-up that is not there; the lesson's 24 pairs gave SCIP 0.88.

options.text: The objective of both runs, since the faster run should also have found more NPV
options.says: A start never changes the optimum: every run in the lesson proved the same value.

origin.section: A Start Is Measured by the Work to a Good Plan, Over Seeds and Cycles

questions.stem: A nightly service stops HiGHS after 50 LP iterations and publishes whatever plan it has; on weekends it lets the same models run to proof. On the lesson's regional plans, what does a repaired start from last cycle change?

options.text: The weekend proofs get much shorter, while the nightly plan stays about as good
options.says: The work to proof was 1.00 with the start against none; the nightly plan is what improved.

options.text: Both the nightly plan and the weekend proofs improve by about the same amount
options.says: Only the plan in hand improved (24% to 4.2% from optimal); the proof work did not change.

options.text: The nightly plan is far closer to optimal, while the weekend proofs take as long
options.says: Right: after 50 LP iterations the plan in hand was 4.2% from optimal with the start and 24% without, and the proof work was unchanged.

options.text: Neither one changes, since HiGHS drops a start carried from an earlier cycle
options.says: HiGHS accepted the repaired start ('MIP start solution is feasible'); it rejected only the carried one.

origin.section: A Start Is Insurance for a Solve That Is Stopped Early
